713969.t: Of unknown origin. A derivation from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰr-ono-, from *ǵʰer- (“to seize, enclose”), has been suggested, with original connotation of "encompassing time-limit".

713964.t: From χρίω (khrī́ō, “to rub, smear; anoint”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix), forming a verbal adjective denoting a resultant state (“fit for spreading or anointing; anointed”), often functioning semantically like a participle.

713975.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *kʰrūsós, cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀬𐀰 (ku-ru-so); further borrowed from a Semitic source, usually assumed to be Phoenician/Punic; compare Phoenician 𐤇𐤓𐤑 (ḥrṣ), Biblical Hebrew חָרוּץ (ḥārûṣ), Akkadian 𒆬𒄀 (ḫurāṣum).

713923.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰórtos (“enclosure”). Cognates include Sanskrit गृह (gṛhá), Latin hortus, and Old English ġeard (English yard).

713915.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰorós, likely from a Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰoros, from a root *ǵʰer-, though the semantic identity of this root has been disputed: * From *ǵʰer- (“to seize, catch, enclose”), with some original meaning of "encircling/ring (dance)",…

713984.t: From χύδην (khúdēn, “as if poured, in abundance”), adverb from the root of χέω (khéō, “to pour”) + -δην (-dēn), + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

713907.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰerH- (“bowel”), but the exact formation is unclear.

713900.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰolā́, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰolh₃-éh₂, from *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”).

713982.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰrṓwmə, and related to χρώς (khrṓs, “surface of the body, skin (color)”); see there for more.

713989.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰutrom, from *ǵʰew- (“to pour”), whence χέω (khéō, “to pour out”); the original meaning was perhaps a "container of liquids (poured things)". Cognate with Sanskrit होत्र (hotrá).

713942.t: Nominal formation from the root of χράομαι (khráomai), χρεώ (khreṓ, “to need”), and χρή (khrḗ, “have to, ought”); see the latter for more.

713985.t: Traditionally derived as a nominal formation from χέω (khéō, “to pour”), but like χυμός (khūmós, “juice, liquid”), it is unclear how the long -υ- (-ū-) can be explained.

713965.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʰrey(H)- (“to smear, strike”), which is perhaps extended from *gʰer- (“to rub”).

713948.t: Formed from the base of χράομαι (khrắomai, “want, need”) + -μα (-mă).

713963.t: From χρίω (khríō, “to rub, smear”) + -μα (-ma). Later form of χρῖμα (khrîma) (LSJ).

713999.t: Seemingly, a formation with the suffix -λός (-lós) like στρεβλός (streblós) and τυφλός (tuphlós), but without obvious etymology.

713937.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₂w- (“to rush in, attack”). Cognate with Latin ingruō (“to attack”), Lithuanian griáuti (“to destroy”), griū́ti (“to crumble”).

713953.t: From the root of χράομαι (khráomai, “to use, desire”) + -ιμος (-imos, “-able, -like”).

713946.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁-, *ǵʰreh₁- (“to desire, need”), with relation to other roots uncertain.

713986.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰumə, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéwmn̥, from *ǵʰew- (“to pour”), whence χέω (khéō).

713983.t: Related to χρῶμα (khrôma), of uncertain origin. According to Beekes, probably cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀫𐀸𐀁 (a-ko-ro-we-e) (representing either /akʰroweʰe/ [dual noun] “without spots”, or /ha-kʰroweʰe/ “of one color”).

713914.t: Uncertain. Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰer-, the same root of χορδή (khordḗ, “guts, intestine”) and Latin hernia (“protruded viscus”).

713930.t: Derived from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰew-. Doublet of χέω (khéō, “to pour”).

713939.t: There is no exact outer-Greek correspondance to the verb, but the root *gʰrem- (“to resound, thunder, grumble, roar”) is Proto-Indo-European.

713919.t: From χόρτος (khórtos, “fodder”) + -άζω (-ázō, suffix to form a verb).

713972.t: From χρυσός (khrūsós, “gold”) + -ιον (-ĭon, “diminutive suffix”). See χρυσός (khrusós) for further etymology.

713962.t: From χρίω (khríō, “to rub, smear, anoint”) + -σις (-sis), forming an action noun.
